If validation fails, the system automatically triggers a repair loop with the failure logs Kimi K2.6 Agent Swarm Tutorial — How to Use 300 Parallel AI Agentsaviralpublic/agentharness.

 SYSTEM SPECIFICATION: KIMI K2.6 MULTIAGENT SWARM ORCHESTRATOR

Construct a distributed multiagent swarm orchestration system using the Moonshot AI Kimi K2.6 API [Kimi K2.6 Agent Swarm Tutorial — How to Use 300
Parallel AI Agents]( ""). The system must coordinate up to 300 domainspecialized subagents  executing up to 4,000 parallel steps  to complete complex, longhorizon software engineering and knowledgeretrieval tasks without task drift .



 SECTION 1: ARCHITECTURAL TOPOLOGY

The system implements a hierarchical ThreeTier Swarm Architecture consisting of an Orchestrator (Parent Session), DomainSpecialized SubAgents, and an Output Aggregation layer .

 1. Parent Orchestrator Node
The core coordinator manages the lifecycle of the swarm . It has three primary components:
 Decomposition Engine: Takes the global user prompt, analyzes dependencies, and compiles the overall objective into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) representing subtasks .
 Dynamic Scheduler: Manages the task execution queue, allocates tasks to subagents, controls ratelimiting and concurrency, and handles staggered launches .
 State Ledger & Memory: Persists the session state, subagent metadata, execution transcripts, and results in a local graph database .

 2. DomainSpecialized SubAgents (Max 300)
Subagents are initialized dynamically based on the DAG plan . They operate with distinct system instructions, local memory contexts, and specialized tool suites . The swarm is categorized into four primary squads :
 Architect Squad (1 Agent): Analyzes architectural design, defines file trees, manages system rules, and maintains technical conventions .
 Frontend Squad (Up to 120 Agents): Generates layouts, interface structures, design styles, and interactive user flows in parallel .
 Backend Squad (Up to 100 Agents): Implements server logic, constructs database schemas, configures API routes, and integrates external authentication and payment services .
 QA Hive & Reviewers (Up to 79 Agents): Runs unit tests, performs realtime code validation, checks for security regressions, and verifies logic across completed modules .

 3. Output Aggregation Layer
 Dependency Resolver: Restructures code changes and artifacts using a logical dependency tree to avoid merge conflicts .
 EvidenceGate Validator: Runs linting, typechecking, and compilation tasks to ensure changes are verified prior to integration .
 Document & Asset Builder: Combines textual outputs, codebases, or analytical findings into finalized, structured formats such as directory trees, slides, or Excel spreadsheets .



 SECTION 2: STEPBYSTEP BUILD AND EXECUTION PIPELINE

 Step 1: Input Analysis and DAG Compilation
Upon receiving a prompt, compile the task objective into a machinereadable JSON execution plan containing:
 A list of tasks with clear ID markers.
 Required agent profiles (Architect, Coder, Reviewer, Tester) .
 I/O definitions (files read/written, parameters passed) .
 A strict dependency array defining execution order .

 Step 2: Session and Workspace Isolation
For coding tasks, initialize an isolated Git worktree or workspace directory . Maintain strict boundary separation so subagents only manipulate authorized file paths . Set up a local tracking database (e.g., .swarm/runs/ directory) to store all decisions, active agent state maps, and logs .

 Step 3: SubAgent Spawning and Initialization
The scheduler spawns subagents concurrently up to the defined resource limits . Initialize each subagent by invoking the Kimi K2.6 model (moonshotai/kimi-k2.6) via the API . 
Set the following hyperparameters in the API payload :
 reasoning_effort: Set to high for complex reasoning and planning tasks, or none for fast execution .
 max_tokens: Configure up to 32,768 output tokens .
 swarm: Pass parameters defining subagent count limits .

Initialize the subagent’s context window with the system prompt, target subtask parameters, and shared architectural guidelines .

 Step 4: Batch Scheduling and RateLimit Management
Implement a scheduler that manages parallel execution . The scheduler must handle ratelimiting constraints using the following mechanisms :
 Staggered Launch: Offset API calls to prevent sudden traffic spikes from overwhelming the endpoint .
 Normalizing Errors: Catch and parse provider ratelimit status codes (e.g., HTTP 429) via an error normalization layer .
 Suspension Events: When rate limits are reached, trigger a suspension event, serialize the subagent's state, and release its slot .
 Adaptive Retry: Automatically resume suspended tasks after backoff delays using preserved subagent IDs and metadata to maintain progress .

 Step 5: Sequential Execution, Tool Use, and Feedback Loops
Allow active subagents to perform tool calls (such as file reads, browser operations, and shell execution) autonomously . Maintain a realtime tracking interface showing progress statuses : queued, running, suspended, completed, failed, or retrying . 

If a subagent encounters an error, route the failure back to the scheduler . The scheduler will reassign the task, invoke a repair subagent, or escalate the issue back to the parent orchestrator .

 Step 6: Evidence Gates and Merging
As subagents finish tasks, they must publish their outputs to the Aggregator .
 The system routes the generated code through validation workflows .
 Tester agents run unit testing and typechecking scripts .
 If validation succeeds, the coordinator merges the code into the master workspace tree . If validation fails, the system automatically triggers a repair loop with the failure logs .

 Step 7: Final Assembly and Output Delivery
After all DAG nodes reach a terminal state, compile the workspace and display the results . Deliver the output in specified project files (such as a fullstack code repository, formatted analytical spreadsheets, or documents) and present the execution logs to the user .



 SECTION 3: API CONTRACTS AND SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE

A kérdésed lényege: hogyan implementálj egy Kimi K2.6alapú, natív 300 subagentes swarm orchestrátort a Requesty router APIdon keresztül, az OpenAIkompatibilis klienseddel. Részletes, productionready megvalósítást adok.

 A Requesty vs. Natív Moonshot API különbség

A natív Moonshot APIn a swarm paraméter közvetlenül beágyazható az API payloadba. A Requesty routeren ez proxyn keresztül megy, ezért az extra swarmspecifikus paramétereket az extra_body mezőn keresztül kell átadni az OpenAI SDKval . Az alapvető model neve a Requesty routeren moonshot/kimi-k2.6 (nem moonshotai/), ahogy a te kódodban is szerepel.

 A SwarmParaméter Átadása Requestyn Keresztül

python
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshot/kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[...],
    extra_body={
        "reasoning_effort": "high",  # vagy "none" gyors taskokhoz
        "swarm": {
            "max_sub_agents": 300,
            "max_steps": 4000
        }
    },
    max_tokens=32768
)


 A Teljes Orchestrátor Implementáció

Az alábbi architektúra a három réteget (Orchestrator → SubAgent Swarm → Aggregator) valósítja meg, a Kimi K2.6 natív swarmképességének kihasználásával.[1][2]

python
import os
import asyncio
import json
import time
import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger("KimiSwarm")

# ─── Konfiguráció ───────────────────────────────────────────────
REQUESTY_API_KEY = os.environ["REQUESTY_API_KEY"]
BASE_URL = "https://router.requesty.ai/v1"
MODEL = "moonshot/kimi-k2.6"

AGENT_ROLES = {
    "architect":  {"max_instances": 1,   "reasoning": "high"},
    "frontend":   {"max_instances": 120, "reasoning": "none"},
    "backend":    {"max_instances": 100, "reasoning": "none"},
    "qa":         {"max_instances": 79,  "reasoning": "high"},
}

SCHEDULER = {
    "stagger_ms":    150,
    "timeout_sec":   600,
    "max_retries":   5,
    "max_concurrent": 50,  # Requesty rate-limit-barát érték
}

# ─── Állapotok ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
class AgentStatus(Enum):
    QUEUED = "queued"
    RUNNING = "running"
    SUSPENDED = "suspended"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    RETRYING = "retrying"

@dataclass
class SubAgentTask:
    id: str
    role: str
    system_prompt: str
    user_prompt: str
    dependencies: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    status: AgentStatus = AgentStatus.QUEUED
    result: str | None = None
    retries: int = 0
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

# ─── DAG Compiler ────────────────────────────────────────────────
class DAGCompiler:
    """Az Orchestrator Decomposition Engine-je: promptból DAG-ot épít."""
    
    def __init__(self, client: AsyncOpenAI):
        self.client = client
    
    async def compile(self, user_goal: str) -> list[SubAgentTask]:
        logger.info("DAG kompilálás...")
        
        dag_prompt = f"""
Te egy swarm orchestrátor vagy. A felhasználó célját elemezd,
és adj vissza egy JSON execution plan-t ezzel a struktúrával:
{{
  "tasks": [
    {{
      "id": "task_001",
      "role": "architect|frontend|backend|qa",
      "system_prompt": "...",
      "user_prompt": "...",
      "dependencies": []
    }}
  ]
}}
Legfeljebb 300 task. A 'dependencies' tartalmaz más task ID-kat.
Cél: {user_goal}
"""
        response = await self.client.chat.completions.create(
            model=MODEL,
            messages=[
                {"role": "system", "content": "DAG compiler orchestrator"},
                {"role": "user",   "content": dag_prompt}
            ],
            extra_body={"reasoning_effort": "high"},
            max_tokens=32768,
            response_format={"type": "json_object"}
        )
        
        raw = json.loads(response.choices[0].message.content)
        tasks = []
        for t in raw.get("tasks", []):
            tasks.append(SubAgentTask(
                id=t["id"], role=t["role"],
                system_prompt=t["system_prompt"],
                user_prompt=t["user_prompt"],
                dependencies=t.get("dependencies", [])
            ))
        logger.info(f"DAG kész: {len(tasks)} task")
        return tasks

# ─── Sub-Agent Runner ────────────────────────────────────────────
class SubAgentRunner:
    """Egyetlen sub-agent végrehajtása a Kimi K2.6 swarm paraméterekkel."""
    
    def __init__(self, client: AsyncOpenAI):
        self.client = client
    
    async def run(self, task: SubAgentTask) -> str:
        role_cfg = AGENT_ROLES.get(task.role, {"reasoning": "none"})
        
        response = await self.client.chat.completions.create(
            model=MODEL,
            messages=[
                {"role": "system", "content": task.system_prompt},
                {"role": "user",   "content": task.user_prompt}
            ],
            extra_body={
                "reasoning_effort": role_cfg["reasoning"],
                "swarm": {
                    "max_sub_agents": 300,
                    "max_steps": 4000
                }
            },
            max_tokens=32768,
            timeout=SCHEDULER["timeout_sec"]
        )
        return response.choices[0].message.content

# ─── Scheduler ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
class SwarmScheduler:
    """
    DAG-alapú párhuzamos ütemező:
    - Staggered launch (rate-limit védelem)
    - HTTP 429 → exponential backoff + suspend/retry
    - Dependency-tracking: csak akkor indul el egy task,
      ha az összes függősége COMPLETED
    """
    
    def __init__(self, client: AsyncOpenAI):
        self.runner = SubAgentRunner(client)
        self.semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(SCHEDULER["max_concurrent"])
        self.results: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.state_ledger: dict[str, AgentStatus] = {}
    
    async def execute_task(self, task: SubAgentTask) -> None:
        task.status = AgentStatus.RUNNING
        self.state_ledger[task.id] = AgentStatus.RUNNING
        
        for attempt in range(SCHEDULER["max_retries"]):
            try:
                async with self.semaphore:
                    # Staggered launch: minden task kicsit késleltetve indul
                    await asyncio.sleep(SCHEDULER["stagger_ms"] / 1000 * attempt)
                    result = await self.runner.run(task)
                
                task.result = result
                task.status = AgentStatus.COMPLETED
                self.results[task.id] = result
                self.state_ledger[task.id] = AgentStatus.COMPLETED
                logger.info(f"✅ {task.id} ({task.role}) kész")
                return
                
            except Exception as e:
                err_str = str(e)
                # Rate-limit kezelés
                if "429" in err_str or "rate" in err_str.lower():
                    backoff = 2 ** attempt
                    logger.warning(f"⏸ {task.id} rate-limit, {backoff}s backoff...")
                    task.status = AgentStatus.SUSPENDED
                    self.state_ledger[task.id] = AgentStatus.SUSPENDED
                    await asyncio.sleep(backoff)
                    task.status = AgentStatus.RETRYING
                    self.state_ledger[task.id] = AgentStatus.RETRYING
                else:
                    logger.error(f"❌ {task.id} hiba: {e}")
                    if attempt == SCHEDULER["max_retries"] - 1:
                        task.status = AgentStatus.FAILED
                        self.state_ledger[task.id] = AgentStatus.FAILED
                        self.results[task.id] = f"FAILED: {e}"
    
    async def run_dag(self, tasks: list[SubAgentTask]) -> dict[str, str]:
        """DAG topológiai sorrendben hajtja végre a taskokat."""
        task_map = {t.id: t for t in tasks}
        pending = set(t.id for t in tasks)
        running_futures: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}
        
        while pending or running_futures:
            # Kész függőségű taskokat indítjuk
            ready = [
                tid for tid in pending
                if all(
                    task_map[dep].status == AgentStatus.COMPLETED
                    for dep in task_map[tid].dependencies
                    if dep in task_map
                )
            ]
            
            for tid in ready:
                pending.discard(tid)
                fut = asyncio.create_task(self.execute_task(task_map[tid]))
                running_futures[tid] = fut
            
            if running_futures:
                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(
                    running_futures.values(),
                    return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
                )
                for f in done:
                    finished = [k for k, v in running_futures.items() if v == f]
                    for k in finished:
                        del running_futures[k]
            elif not ready:
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        
        return self.results

# ─── Output Aggregator ───────────────────────────────────────────
class OutputAggregator:
    """Validálja és összefésüli a sub-agent outputokat."""
    
    def __init__(self, client: AsyncOpenAI):
        self.client = client
    
    async def aggregate(self, results: dict[str, str], original_goal: str) -> str:
        combined = "\n\n".join(
            f"=== {tid} ===\n{output}"
            for tid, output in results.items()
            if not output.startswith("FAILED")
        )
        
        response = await self.client.chat.completions.create(
            model=MODEL,
            messages=[
                {
                    "role": "system",
                    "content": "Te egy aggregátor vagy. Szintetizáld a sub-agent outputokat."
                },
                {
                    "role": "user",
                    "content": f"Eredeti cél: {original_goal}\n\nSub-agent outputok:\n{combined}"
                }
            ],
            extra_body={"reasoning_effort": "high"},
            max_tokens=32768
        )
        return response.choices[0].message.content

# ─── Fő Orchestrátor ────────────────────────────────────────────
class KimiSwarmOrchestrator:
    """
    Háromrétegű swarm orchestrátor:
    Orchestrator → DAG Scheduler → Sub-Agent Swarm → Aggregator
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.client = AsyncOpenAI(
            api_key=REQUESTY_API_KEY,
            base_url=BASE_URL
        )
        self.dag_compiler  = DAGCompiler(self.client)
        self.scheduler     = SwarmScheduler(self.client)
        self.aggregator    = OutputAggregator(self.client)
    
    async def run(self, user_goal: str) -> str:
        logger.info(f"🚀 Swarm elindítva: {user_goal[:80]}...")
        
        # 1. DAG összeállítása
        tasks = await self.dag_compiler.compile(user_goal)
        
        # 2. Parallel végrehajtás DAG-sorrendben
        results = await self.scheduler.run_dag(tasks)
        
        # Státusz összesítő
        completed = sum(1 for s in self.scheduler.state_ledger.values()
                        if s == AgentStatus.COMPLETED)
        failed    = sum(1 for s in self.scheduler.state_ledger.values()
                        if s == AgentStatus.FAILED)
        logger.info(f"📊 Befejezett: {completed}, Sikertelen: {failed}")
        
        # 3. Aggregálás és végeredmény
        final = await self.aggregator.aggregate(results, user_goal)
        return final


# ─── Belépési pont ───────────────────────────────────────────────
async def main():
    orchestrator = KimiSwarmOrchestrator()
    result = await orchestrator.run(
        "Építs egy teljes full-stack task manager appot React frontendel "
        "és FastAPI backendel, autentikációval, PostgreSQL adatbázissal."
    )
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())


 Kritikus Implementációs Részletek

extra_body vs. natív Moonshot API: Az OpenAI SDK nem ismeri a swarm és reasoning_effort paramétereket alapból, ezért az extra_body dictbe kell csomagolni őket . A natív moonshot Python SDKval ezek első osztályú paraméterek lennének, de a Requesty routeren az extra_body a helyes megközelítés.

Konkurencia korlát: A Requesty API saját ratelimit szabályokat alkalmaz . Az 50es szemafor (asyncio.Semaphore(50)) egy biztonságos kezdőérték; a natív Kimi infrastruktúrán 300 agent futhat párhuzamosan, de a Requesty proxyn érdemes fokozatosan növelni és figyelni a 429es válaszokat.

reasoning_effort stratégia: Az architect és qa agentek "high" értéket kapnak a komplex analitikai munkához, míg a frontend és backend kódoló agentek "none" értéket a gyors, egyenes végrehajtáshoz . Ez jelentősen csökkenti a tokenfelhasználást és a válaszidőt.

DAG topológia: A run_dag metódus dependencyawarenessszel fut: egy backend agent csak akkor indul el, ha az architect agent már befejezett. Ez megakadályozza a task driftet és az inkonzisztens architektúrát .

Workspace izoláció: Production környezetben a SubAgentTask metadata mezőjébe érdemes fájlpath korlátokat beletenni, és minden agent csak a számára engedélyezett .swarm/runs/{task_id}/ könyvtárba írjon .

SYSTEM SPECIFICATION: KIMI K2.6 NATIVE AGENT SWARM INTEGRATION

This specification details how to programmatically implement and invoke the firstparty, native Agent Swarm feature of the Moonshot AI Kimi K2.6 model  through an API router or client.



 SECTION 1: ARCHITECTURAL OVERVIEW

The Kimi K2.6 model features a native, firstparty Agent Swarm orchestration layer built directly into the model's core architecture . Instead of requiring the developer to build, manage, and synchronize a manual Pythonbased multiagent framework, the Kimi K2.6 backend acts as the central coordinator . 

When invoked with the appropriate API configuration, the model autonomously handles:
 Dynamic task decomposition into parallel, heterogeneous subtasks .
 Instantiation and coordination of up to 300 domainspecialized, parallel subagents .
 Horizontal execution across a maximum budget of 4,000 steps .
 Automatic task assignment, active progress tracking, and conflict resolution using a dependency graph .
 Dynamic reassignment of tasks if a subagent fails or becomes stuck .
 Output merging and consolidation into structured files, such as multipage web codebases, documents, or spreadsheets .



 SECTION 2: API CONTRACT AND INTEGRATION PAYLOAD

To trigger Kimi K2.6's native swarm orchestration rather than standard sequential completion, you must pass a specialized agent parameter block in the request payload using the extra_body configuration .

 1. Payload Parameters
 model: Must be configured to a Kimi K2.6 deployment (e.g., moonshot/kimi-k2.6 or kimi-k2.6) .
 agent.type: Explicitly set to "swarm" to activate the native multiagent execution pipeline .
 agent.max_agents: Sets the horizontal scaling limit for the run (up to 300 parallel subagents) .
 agent.max_steps: Specifies the total step budget allocated to the coordinated swarm execution (up to 4000 steps) .

 2. Integration Code Example (Python)
The following code demonstrates how to implement this integration using an OpenAIcompatible client routing through an external API router:

python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

# Initialize client using the custom router base URL and API key
client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["REQUESTY_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://router.requesty.ai/v1",
)

# Define a complex, long-horizon task requiring parallel generation
prompt_content = """
Create a comprehensive full-stack enterprise codebase. 
Decompose this project into a structured database schema, 
a scalable backend system with RESTful API handlers, 
a responsive modern frontend with interactive UI components, 
and a test suite with 100% code coverage.
"""

# Call chat completions with the first-party 'agent' configuration
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshoot/kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user", 
            "content": prompt_content
        }
    ],
    # Native Swarm mode parameter passed in extra_body
    extra_body={
        "agent": {
            "type": "swarm",
            "max_agents": 300,
            "max_steps": 4000
        }
    },
)

# Output the unified aggregated result compiled by the swarm orchestrator
print(response.choices[Kimi K2.6 Agent Swarm: 300 Agents, 4000 Steps - Verdent AI](https://www.verdent.ai/guides/kimi-k2-6-agent-swarm "www.verdent.ai/guides/kimi-k2-6-agent-swarm").message.content)




 SECTION 3: SYSTEM EXECUTION FLOW

When the API router receives this request, the Kimi K2.6 engine processes the instruction through the following execution phases:

 Phase 1: Input Analysis and DAG Compilation
The primary Kimi K2.6 model context processes the system instructions and compiles a machinereadable Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) . This graph details the task dependency array, required agent skills (e.g., frontend, backend, testing), and the precise flow of data inputs and outputs .

 Phase 2: Dynamic SubAgent Allocation
The native coordinator provisions the specialized subagent squads up to the requested max_agents limit (maximum of 300 parallel agents) . In a complete software generation run, these roles typically include:
 The Architect (1 Instance): Designs database schemas and creates project directories .
 The Frontend Squad (up to 120 Instances): Creates layout components, user interfaces, and page routes in parallel .
 The Backend Core (up to 100 Instances): Sets up API endpoints, business logic, and database migrations in parallel .
 The QA Hive & Reviewers (up to 79 Instances): Conducts security checks, linting, code reviews, and executes tests .

 Phase 3: Autonomous Execution, Web Crawling, and Tool Calling
The active subagents run simultaneously to perform target tasks, make tool calls (such as search, document parsing, or code writing), and gather information in parallel .

 Phase 4: Active Conflict Resolution and Dynamic Reassignment
If any subagent runs into a rate limit, experiences an error, or hangs on a task, the firstparty coordinator intervenes . The coordinator serializes the failed task state, releases the slot, and dynamically assigns the work to an idle subagent or triggers an automated repair sequence using error log contexts .

 Phase 5: Dependency Validation and Unified Aggregation
Once subtasks are successfully validated, the engine's internal merging algorithms compile all files, verify design consistency, resolve namespace issues, and compile the final workspace . The unified output is packaged and returned to the client as a single, finalized response payload .

Ez egy rendkívül fontos tisztázás. A hivatalos Moonshot platform dokumentáció alapján a Kimi K2.6 natív Agent Swarm nem egy APIparaméter, amelyet az extra_bodyn keresztül lehet aktiválni. A swarm képesség a modell backend infrastruktúrájába van beépítve, és a Kimi Code CLIn, a Kimi.com felületen, és a Kimi Work desktop appon keresztül érhető el natívan — nem sima chat/completions API hívással.

 A Valóság: Mi Létezik és Mi Nem

A Kimi K2.6 hivatalos API dokumentációja (platform.kimi.ai) sehol nem említ agent.type, swarm, max_agents, vagy max_steps paramétereket a chat/completions endpointon. A dokumentált extra paraméterek: thinking (enabled/disabled), keep (preserve thinking). A Requestyn átmenő hívásod esetén az extra_body={"agent": {"type": "swarm", ...}} szintaxis nagy valószínűséggel egyszerűen figyelmen kívül lesz hagyva, nem dob hibát, de nem is aktivál natív swarmot.[1][2]

A natív 300 subagentes swarm az alkalmazásrétegbe van beépítve: a Kimi Work desktop agent, a Kimi Code CLI, és a kimi.com chat felület tartalmazza azt a külső orchestrátort, amely a modell APIt ismételten hívja, nem maga az API egyetlen végpontja.[3][4]

 Hogyan Működik Valójában a Swarm

A Kimi K2.6 modell agentikus képessége nem egyetlen HTTP kérésből áll, hanem a Kimi Code és Kimi Work alkalmazások végzik el az orchestrációt: fogadják a promptot, belső DAGot építenek, majd egymás után (és párhuzamosan) indítanak el chat/completions kéréseket a modell felé, ahol minden subagent egyegy önálló szession. A modell maga 300ig skálázódó párhuzamos kontextussal bír, de ezt a workflowt az alkalmazásréteg vezényli, nem az API payload.[5][1]

 A Helyes Integráció Requestyn Keresztül

Az általad megadott Requesty setuppal ez a productionready megközelítés:

python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["REQUESTY_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://router.requesty.ai/v1",
)

# ── 1. Thinking MODE (alapértelmezett K2.6 viselkedés) ──────────
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshot/kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a senior software architect."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Design a full-stack task manager app."}
    ],
    max_tokens=32768,
    # NE adj meg temperature/top_p értéket – a K2.6 fixed értékeket használ:
    # thinking mode: temp=1.0, top_p=0.95
    # instant mode: temp=0.6, top_p=0.95
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)

# ── 2. Instant MODE (gyors, reasoning nélkül) ───────────────────
response_instant = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshot/kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Convert 100 USD to EUR."}],
    max_tokens=1024,
    extra_body={
        "thinking": {"type": "disabled"}  # Ez az egyetlen dokumentált extra param
    }
)

# ── 3. Multi-turn preserve thinking (K2.6 exkluzív feature) ─────
response_mt = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshot/kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Analyze this schema and suggest indexes."},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "Based on query patterns..."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Now optimize the slowest query."}
    ],
    extra_body={
        "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "keep": "all"}  # Megőrzi a reasoning contextet
    },
    max_tokens=32768
)


 Swarm Viselkedés Szimulálása Saját Kódban

Ha az alkalmazásodban valóban párhuzamos multiagent orchestrációt szeretnél a Requestyn keresztül, az előző válaszban adott Python architektúra (aszinkron DAG scheduler + asyncio) az egyetlen helyes út. Ez pontosan azt csinálja, amit a Kimi Work/Code belső rendszere tesz: az orchestrációt te végzed, a modell APIt eszközként használva.[4]

python
import asyncio
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

client = AsyncOpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["REQUESTY_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://router.requesty.ai/v1",
)

async def run_sub_agent(task: str, thinking: bool = False) -> str:
    """Egyetlen sub-agent hívás – ezt hívod 300-szor párhuzamosan."""
    response = await client.chat.completions.create(
        model="moonshot/kimi-k2.6",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": task}],
        max_tokens=32768,
        extra_body={
            "thinking": {"type": "enabled" if thinking else "disabled"}
        }
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content

async def swarm(tasks: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """300 sub-agent párhuzamos futtatása."""
    return await asyncio.gather(*[run_sub_agent(t) for t in tasks])


 A Legfontosabb Tények Összefoglalása

| Mit hittünk | Valóság |
|||
| extra_body={"agent": {"type": "swarm"}} aktiválja a natív swarmot | Nem dokumentált, nincs ilyen API paraméter [2] |
| reasoning_effort: "high"/"none" | A K2.6 thinking: {type: "enabled"/"disabled"} paramétert használ [2] |
| Egyetlen API hívás = 300 agent | A swarm az alkalmazásrétegben (Kimi Work/Code) van, nem az APIban [5] |
| max_agents, max_steps paraméterek | Nem léteznek a chat/completions endpointon [2] |
| Requestyn moonshot/kimi-k2.6 | Helyes modellnév [1] |

A valódi 300agentes swarmhoz natívan a Kimi Work desktop appot vagy a Kimi Code CLIt kell használni. Requesty APIn keresztül a saját Python orchestrátorod az egyetlen járható út, amely a chat/completions endpointot hívja ismételten, párhuzamos asyncio taskok formájában.[3][4]
